items.t: Symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea (12 years and over); acute episodes of diarrhoea with irritable bowel syndrome in adults 18 and over after initial diagnosis by a doctor.

src.q: For the symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea in adults and children aged 12 years and over.
For the symptomatic treatment of acute episodes of diarrhoea associated with Irritable Bowel Syndrome in adults aged 18 years and over following initial diagnosis by a doctor.

items.t: Symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea (including acute exacerbations of chronic diarrhoea) for up to 5 days in adults and children over 9 years; chronic diarrhoea in adults.

src.q: For the symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea of any aetiology including acute exacerbations of chronic diarrhoea for periods of up to 5 days in adults and children over 9 years.
For the symptomatic treatment of chronic diarrhoea in adults.

items.t: MHRA: on general sale the maximum daily dose is 12 mg; from pharmacists 16 mg.

src.q: is available on general sale (maximum daily dose 12 mg) and from pharmacists (maximum daily dose 16 mg).

items.t: IBS use: only after IBS has been diagnosed by a doctor.

src.q: Only take this medicine to treat acute episodes of diarrhoea associated with Irritable Bowel Syndrome if your doctor has previously diagnosed IBS.

items.t: Adults and children over 12: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg after each loose stool. Maximum 12 mg (6 capsules) a day.

src.q: Adults and children over 12: 2 capsules (4 mg) initially followed by 1 capsule (2 mg) after every loose stool.
The maximum daily dose should not exceed 6 capsules (12 mg).

items.t: Adults 18 and over: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg after each loose stool. Maximum 12 mg a day.

src.q: Two capsules (4 mg) to be taken initially, followed by 1 capsule (2 mg) after every loose stool, or as previously advised by your doctor.

items.t: Adults and children over 12: 4 mg initially, then 2 mg after each loose stool; usual 6-8 mg a day. Maximum 16 mg (8 capsules) a day.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years: Two capsules (4 mg) initially, followed by one capsule (2 mg) after each loose stool.
The usual dose is 3-4 capsules (6 mg - 8 mg) a day. The total daily dose should not exceed 8 capsules (16 mg).

items.t: Adults: start 4-8 mg a day in divided doses; adjust up to a maximum of 16 mg (8 capsules) a day. Maintenance can be given twice daily.

src.q: The starting dose should be between two and four capsules per day in divided doses, depending on severity.
If required, this dose can be adjusted according to result up to a maximum of eight capsules daily.

items.t: Elderly and renal impairment: no dose adjustment.

src.q: Elderly No dose adjustment is required for the elderly. Renal impairment No dose adjustment is required for patients with renal impairment.

items.t: Pharmacy/general sale capsule: contraindicated under 12 years.

src.q: Imodium is contraindicated in children less than 12 years of age.

items.t: Prescription-only capsule: contraindicated under 9 years. Children 9-12 years: 2 mg four times daily until diarrhoea is controlled (up to 5 days); do not exceed. Investigate if no improvement within 2 days.

src.q: in children less than 9 years of age.
Children 9 to 12 years One capsule (2 mg) four times daily until diarrhoea is controlled (up to 5 days). This dose should not be exceeded.
Further investigation into the cause of the diarrhoea should be considered if there is no improvement within two days of starting treatment with loperamide.

items.t: Children are more sensitive to CNS effects in overdose. Fluid and electrolyte replacement is the priority in young children.

src.q: Children, and patients with hepatic dysfunction, may be more sensitive to CNS effects.
This is particularly important in young children and in frail and elderly patients with acute diarrhoea.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to loperamide or any excipient.

src.q: hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Children under 12 (pharmacy/general sale capsule) or under 9 (prescription-only capsule).

src.q: in children less than 12 years of age.
in children less than 9 years of age.

items.t: Acute dysentery (blood in stools and high fever). The prescription-only capsule SmPC words it as: should not be used alone.

src.q: in patients with acute dysentery, which is characterised by blood in stools and high fever.
Loperamide hydrochloride should not be used alone in acute dysentery

items.t: Acute ulcerative colitis; bacterial enterocolitis from invasive organisms (Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter); pseudomembranous colitis with broad-spectrum antibiotics.

src.q: in patients with acute ulcerative colitis. in patients with bacterial enterocolitis caused by invasive organisms including Salmonella, Shigella and Campylobacter.
in patients with pseudomembranous colitis associated with the use of broad-spectrum antibiotics.

items.t: When inhibition of peristalsis must be avoided (risk of ileus, megacolon, toxic megacolon). Stop promptly if ileus, constipation or abdominal distension develop.

src.q: Imodium must not be used when inhibition of peristalsis is to be avoided due to the possible risk of significant sequelae including ileus, megacolon and toxic megacolon.
Imodium must be discontinued promptly when ileus, constipation or abdominal distension develop.

items.t: Overdose: cardiac events including QT and QRS prolongation and torsades de pointes, some fatal; overdose can unmask Brugada syndrome. Do not exceed the recommended dose or duration.

src.q: Cardiac events including QT interval and QRS complex prolongation and torsades de pointes have been reported in association with overdose. Some cases had a fatal outcome
Overdose can unmask existing Brugada syndrome.
Patients should not exceed the recommended dose and/or the recommended duration of treatment.

items.t: MHRA: serious cardiac events (QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, cardiac arrest), including deaths, with high doses taken as a drug of abuse or to self-treat opioid withdrawal.

src.q: There have been reports of cardiac events including QT prolongation, torsades de pointes, and cardiac arrest in patients who have taken high or very high doses of loperamide as a drug of abuse or for self-treatment of opioid withdrawal.

items.t: History of drug abuse: caution. Loperamide is an opioid; abuse and misuse are described.

src.q: Caution is needed in patients with a history of drug abuse. Abuse and misuse of loperamide, has been described
Loperamide is an opioid with low bioavailability and limited potential to penetrate the blood brain barrier at therapeutic doses.

items.t: Hepatic impairment: use with caution (reduced first-pass metabolism; relative overdose may cause CNS toxicity).

src.q: this medicine should be used with caution in such patients because of reduced first pass metabolism, as it may result in a relative overdose leading to CNS toxicity.

items.t: Acute diarrhoea: no improvement within 48 hours - stop and see a doctor. Persistent diarrhoea needs investigation; replace fluid and electrolytes.

src.q: In acute diarrhoea, if clinical improvement is not observed within 48 hours, the administration of Imodium should be discontinued and patients should be advised to consult their doctor.
Use of this medicine does not preclude the administration of appropriate fluid and electrolyte replacement therapy.

items.t: AIDS: stop at the earliest signs of abdominal distension (toxic megacolon reported with infectious colitis).

src.q: Patients with AIDS treated with this medicine for diarrhoea should have therapy stopped at the earliest signs of abdominal distension.

items.t: Galactose intolerance, lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption: should not take (contains lactose).

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption should not take this medicine because it contains lactose.

items.t: P-glycoprotein inhibitors (quinidine, ritonavir): 2-3-fold higher loperamide levels; clinical relevance at usual doses unknown.

src.q: Concomitant administration of loperamide (16 mg single dose) with quinidine, or ritonavir, which are both P-glycoprotein inhibitors, resulted in a 2 to 3-fold increase in loperamide plasma levels.

items.t: Itraconazole (3-4-fold), ketoconazole (5-fold) and gemfibrozil (about 2-fold) raise loperamide levels; itraconazole plus gemfibrozil gave a 13-fold rise in exposure. No CNS effects were seen in these studies.

src.q: resulted in a 3 to 4-fold increase in loperamide plasma concentrations
The combination of itraconazole and gemfibrozil resulted in a 4-fold increase in peak plasma levels of loperamide and a 13-fold increase in total plasma exposure.

items.t: Oral desmopressin: plasma levels rose 3-fold (slower gut motility).

src.q: Concomitant treatment with oral desmopressin resulted in a 3-fold increase of desmopressin plasma concentrations, presumably due to slower gastrointestinal motility.

items.t: Drugs with similar pharmacology may potentiate loperamide; drugs that speed GI transit may reduce its effect.

src.q: It is expected that drugs with similar pharmacological properties may potentiate loperamide's effect and that drugs that accelerate gastrointestinal transit may decrease its effect.

items.t: No dose adjustment required.

src.q: Renal impairment No dose adjustment is required for patients with renal impairment.

items.t: No pharmacokinetic data. Use with caution: reduced first-pass metabolism may cause relative overdose and CNS toxicity (one UK SmPC gives severe hepatic disturbance as an example).

src.q: Although no pharmacokinetic data are available in patients with hepatic impairment, this medicine should be used with caution in such patients because of reduced first pass metabolism
(eg in cases of severe hepatic disturbance)

items.t: SmPC: safety not established (no teratogenicity in animals); not advisable in pregnancy, especially the first trimester.

src.q: As with other drugs, it is not advisable to administer this medicine in pregnancy, especially during the first trimester.

items.t: BUMPS: only recommended in pregnancy if there is no suitable alternative; it is unclear whether there is any risk.

src.q: loperamide is only recommended during pregnancy if there is no suitable alternative, as there is not enough information to say it is safe for the baby.
It is unclear if there is any risk.

items.t: Small amounts may pass into breast milk: not recommended during breastfeeding.

src.q: Small amounts of loperamide may appear in human breast milk. Therefore, this medicine is not recommended during breast-feeding.

reproductive.note: UK SmPCs: effect on human fertility not evaluated.

items.t: Most common (1% or more): constipation, flatulence, headache, nausea.

src.q: constipation (2.7%), flatulence (1.7%), headache (1.2%) and nausea (1.1%)

items.t: Ileus (including paralytic), megacolon including toxic megacolon: stop promptly if constipation, distension or ileus develop.

src.q: Ileusa (including paralytic ileus) Megacolona (including toxic megacolonb)

items.t: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, bullous eruptions (including SJS, TEN, erythema multiforme).

src.q: Bullous eruptiona (including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, Toxic epidermal necrolysis and Erythema multiforme)

items.t: Overdose: CNS depression (including respiratory depression), urinary retention, ileus; QT/QRS prolongation, ventricular arrhythmias, cardiac arrest, deaths. Start ECG monitoring; naloxone is the antidote and may need repeating; observe at least 48 hours.

src.q: In cases of overdose, ECG monitoring for QT interval prolongation should be initiated.
If CNS symptoms of overdose occur, naloxone can be given as an antidote.
the patient should be monitored closely for at least 48 hours in order to detect possible CNS depression.

src.q: if clinical improvement is not observed within 48 hours, the administration of Imodium should be discontinued

items.t: Overdose: ECG monitoring for QT prolongation; observe for CNS depression for at least 48 hours.

src.q: patients should be monitored closely for at least 48 hours to detect possible CNS depression
In cases of overdose, ECG monitoring for QT interval prolongation should be initiated.

items.t: Oral; take capsules with liquid.

src.q: The capsules should be taken with liquid.

items.t: Never take more than the recommended dose on the label.

src.q: pharmacists should remind patients not to take more than the recommended dose on the label

items.t: May cause tiredness, dizziness or drowsiness: take care driving or using machines.

src.q: Loss of consciousness, depressed level of consciousness, tiredness, dizziness, or drowsiness may occur when diarrhoea is treated with this medicine.

items.t: Keep up fluid and electrolyte replacement; see a doctor if no better in 48 hours.

src.q: The priority in acute diarrhoea is the prevention or reversal of fluid and electrolyte depletion.
